profile.campus: Ashburn, Loudoun County, Virginia (Equinix Ashburn campus, Data Center Alley)
profile.reading:
This building operates as Equinix's DC4 data center at 21691 Filigree Court in Ashburn, Virginia, one node in Equinix's cluster of buildings spread across Loudoun County's Data Center Alley. Equinix's own DC4 facility page publishes concrete numbers rather than general marketing text, 60,590 square feet of space, N+2 power redundancy, and eight compliance certifications, HIPAA, ISO 9001, ISO 22301, ISO 27001, NIST 800-53/FISMA High, PCI DSS, SOC 1 Type II, and SOC 2 Type II. N+2 power redundancy is a step above the N+1 power redundancy Equinix publishes for its DC6 and DC16 buildings nearby on this same campus, though Equinix does not publish an IT load or utility power figure in megawatts for DC4 itself, so this entry does not assign one.

Ashburn's status as the center of Data Center Alley predates Equinix's arrival. AOL built what is generally regarded as the area's first data center, its Dulles Technology Center, in 1997 to support its dial up internet subscriber base, and the fiber capacity that project pulled into Loudoun County helped seed the cluster of interconnected facilities that followed. Equinix opened its own first Ashburn building, DC1, in the late 1990s, and its second building, DC2, earned a reputation, per Data Center Dynamics, as one of the most connected buildings on earth. Loudoun County's data center corridor has since grown into what Data Center Dynamics describes as roughly 10 million square feet of built space consuming on the order of 1 gigawatt of electrical power region wide, a figure covering every operator in the corridor rather than Equinix alone.

Equinix's own Washington D.C. metro listing page currently names and links 15 facilities together, DC1 through DC6, DC10 through DC16, DC21, and DC22, with most addresses in Ashburn and at least one, DC14, in nearby Manassas. Equinix does not publish a combined power or square footage total for that group of buildings, and Equinix markets DC1 through DC6 and DC10 through DC12 collectively as offering access to one of the top three internet peering exchange markets on the East Coast, without singling out DC4's own peering density or customer roster.

Every data center on this campus now also sits inside Virginia's evolving electricity regulatory framework for large power users. The State Corporation Commission approved new Dominion Energy rates in November 2026 that raise a typical residential bill by about 16 dollars a month, while creating a new GS-5 rate class specifically for data centers, effective January 1, 2027, that requires large demand customers like Equinix's Ashburn buildings to sign 14 year minimum contracts with cost coverage guarantees, according to Inside Climate News's reporting on the commission's decision.

reading.body:
Equinix DC4 is a 60,590-square-foot facility in Ashburn, Virginia, part of Equinix's multi-building Ashburn campus in Data Center Alley, Loudoun County. The operator publishes no power capacity figure for this specific building. Equinix's DC2 building on the same campus, cited as representative of campus general specifications, supports a minimum cabinet density of 4 kilovolt-amperes, which at typical AI training loads of 40 kilowatts per rack would imply roughly 10 racks per cabinet; the actual IT load and accelerator count at DC4 remain unknown without published power data.

Data Center Alley in Loudoun County is described as the greatest concentration of data center space on the planet at roughly 10 million square feet. Equinix's Ashburn campus anchors one of the top three internet peering exchange markets on the US East Coast. Virginia's 330 mapped data center facilities represent a major regional cluster, though only 23 publish power capacity figures; those 23 facilities account for 1,375 megawatts of published capacity statewide, and this campus ranks 24th by published megawatts, below the threshold of public disclosure in Virginia's current data.

The facility holds certifications including HIPAA, ISO 27001, SOC 2 Type II, and NIST 800-53/FISMA High, though these are confirmed only for DC2 as representative of campus general specifications and not explicitly published for DC4 itself. Without published power figures or building-specific certifications, DC4's significance to AI scaling cannot be directly assessed from Equinix's public specification page, though its location in Data Center Alley and its position within a campus serving a top-three peering market on the East Coast places it in one of the continent's most strategically connected data center regions.
